title: What is known about 1RB1LD_1RC0RC_1LD0RE_0LB0LA_0RF1LA_---1RC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LD_1RC0RC_1LD0RE_0LB0LA_0RF1LA_---1RC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. After step 731,206 the left end of the tape never moves again. The head bounces between a turning point well inside the tape and the right end. On each round trip, nothing left of the turning point is visited, and everything right of a point just past it is shifted right by exactly two cells, unchanged. So the only cells a trip really rewrites lie in a small window at the turning point: about 30 cells typically, at most about a thousand in the first 2·1010 steps. The turning point drifts right at about 0.4 of the tape's width, leaving an untouched archive behind it.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 30,011 cells have been visited and 19,605 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.514).

claims.title: The stream is translated rigidly
claims.text: Between consecutive arrivals of the head at the right end, the tape right of a boundary cell is exactly the previous tape shifted right by 2 cells. This held for 436 of 436 round trips between steps 10<sup>8</sup> and 1.2·10<sup>8</sup>, with the boundary between cells 3,446 and 3,817 of a tape of 9,467 to 10,339 cells.

claims.title: The generator grows too
claims.text: For 39 round trips after each of 10<sup>6</sup>, 10<sup>7</sup>, 10<sup>8</sup> and 10<sup>9</sup> steps, the tape is 1,105, 3,161, 9,467 and 30,011 cells wide. The boundary of the rigid part lies between cells 777–808, 1,532–1,572, 3,446–3,531 and 11,845–11,890. In the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps the left end of the tape is last extended at step 731,206.

claims.title: Why it is hard
claims.text: The head drifts across the stream in a short local zigzag, not over a repeated word, so the shift rules used for other holdouts do not apply directly. The generator region has no visible block structure. The machine halts only when E reads 0 with a 0 to its right (F reading 0 is its only undefined transition). Whether the generator ever produces that is open.

claims.title: The halting situations
claims.text: E>0 0 halts after one step, C>1 0 0 after two, B>0 1 0 0 and B>1 1 0 0 after three: F is entered only from E on a 0, E only from C on a 1, C only from B or F, all moving right.

claims.title: Only a small window is rewritten
claims.text: At every 20th round trip up to step 2·10<sup>10</sup> (3,444 samples), the cells a trip rewrites lie between its turning point and a point z past which the tape is the previous one shifted right by two. The window from the turning point to z has median width 27 to 30 cells, 99th percentile about 450, largest 1,054. The turning point is at 0.37 to 0.41 of the tape's width.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The open part is the window: what it writes to the archive and the stream, and what it reads back from them.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine only ever rewrites a few dozen cells at a time, at one wandering spot; left of it the tape lies untouched, right of it everything slides two cells per round trip. This page runs it in your browser.

facts.text: Median width of the window a round trip rewrites (largest seen: 1,054).
The stream right of the window moves two cells per round trip, unchanged.
No halt in the C simulator.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.514).
After 109 steps the tape spans 30,011 cells (496 left of the start, 21,252 right), with a density of 1s of 0.653.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A generator and a conveyor
html: Follow the head after step 108. It runs from the right end of the tape back to about cell 3,400–3,600 in a tight zigzag (about 3.6 steps per cell), and then all the way back. One round trip takes about 43,000 steps.

Compare the tape at two consecutive arrivals at the right end. Beyond a boundary near the turning point, the new tape is the old one shifted right by exactly two cells, with no other change. This held for all 436 round trips between steps 108 and 1.2·108. So the right part of the tape is a conveyor: whatever the region near the turning point produces is carried off to the right and never touched again.
The stream itself looks irregular. A piece of it at step 100,130,996, cells 6,001–6,100:

sections.heading: A small window between an archive and a stream
html: Compare the tape at the end of one round trip with the tape at the end of the previous one. Left of the trip's turning point nothing changed: the head never went there. Right of a point a little past the turning point the tape is the old one shifted two cells to the right. Only the window between them was rewritten, and it is small. Its width at every 60th round trip up to step 2·1010:
Most of the time the window is a few dozen cells; now and then a trip reaches a few hundred cells further. The turning point drifts to the right at about 0.4 of the tape's width:

That drift is an average. From one trip to the next the turning point jumps by tens to hundreds of cells either way (most often −4, −1, −11, +6 or +3 cells, up to about ±400), with no visible period in the jumps or in the window widths.

So the tape has three parts: an archive left of the turning point, written by the window as it passed and read again only when the turning point moves back over it; the window; and the stream, carried away two cells per trip. What a trip into the stream brings back depends mostly on the cells next to the window: at one fixed cell, among the trips of steps 108 to 4·108, the state the head comes back in is a function of the state it left in and the 28 cells around it for all but one of 779 different such windows (c/returns.c).

sections.heading: Both parts grow

The tape grows by two cells per round trip, so its width grows like the square root of the time. The generator, left of the boundary, keeps roughly 40% of it.

sections.heading: What would decide it
html: The conveyor is harmless: the stream is only copied. Everything rests on the generator, and the machine halts only when E reads 0 with a 0 to its right. A next step would be the transducer of one sweep across the stream, as rules on short words, proved in Lean. Then one could study the generator as a map from one round trip to the next.

summary: The head bounces between a turning point and the right end; each round trip rewrites only a small window (median about 30 cells) at the turning point, leaves everything to its left untouched and carries everything to its right two cells further, unchanged. Open.
family: small active window between an untouched archive and a rigidly translated stream (F08)
